title: v3.1.0 repeats the vendor's apply-the-latest-CRDs note — no CRD schema changed between v3.0.0 and v3.1.0

detection.reason: nothing in the CRD files changed for this release (git diff v3.0.0..v3.1.0 over config/crd and helm crds is empty); recorded so the vendor's boilerplate is visibly accounted for, the hint names the LBC CRDs

quote: Action : Please apply the latest CRD definitions
remediation: No CRD change ships in 3.1.0 (the Global Accelerator cross-namespace feature is code-only). Re-applying the CRDs is harmless; the 3.2 and 3.5 rules carry the real schema changes.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd targetgroupbindings.elbv2.k8s.aws -o json | jq -r '[.spec.versions[] | select(.served) | .name] as $v | (.spec.versions[] | select(.storage) | .schema.openAPIV3Schema.properties.spec.properties // {} | keys) as $k | "served=\($v | join(",")) spec fields=\($k | join(","))"'  # the installed CRD schema; nothing new absent from the field list means the CRDs were not re-applied for this release
coversNotes: v3.1.0 (If using Gateway API fea): Standard Gateway API CRDs: kubectl apply -f https://github.co
chart value added: keepTLSSecret = false — keepTLSSecret: false

title: HTTPRequestRedirect without a port now defaults to 80/443 from the scheme (Gateway API conformance) — redirects that relied on the listener port change

detection.reason: only a RequestRedirect on a route an LBC ALB Gateway serves changes, and the projection cannot tie one route's filter to its parent's controller in one predicate; the hint names the HTTPRoutes whose Gateway class is the ALB controller's (a redirect on a Traefik or other Gateway is not the LBC's)

quote: [ALB Gateway] Port defaulting for scheme - Fixed redirect port handling to comply with Gateway API spec. When port is not specified in HTTPRequestRedirectFilter, the controller correctly defaults to well-known ports (80 for http, 443 for https) based on the redirect scheme.
remediation: Review HTTPRoute RequestRedirect filters that set scheme but no port on a non-standard listener port: the Location header now carries the well-known port of the scheme. Set filters[].requestRedirect.port explicitly to keep the old target.
verifyCommand: kubectl get gatewayclasses,gateways,httproutes -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items as $i | [$i[] | select(.kind == "GatewayClass" and .spec.controllerName == "gateway.k8s.aws/alb") | .metadata.name] as $c | [$i[] | select(.kind == "Gateway" and (.spec.gatewayClassName | IN($c[]))) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name] as $g | $i[] | select(.kind == "HTTPRoute") | .metadata.namespace as $ns | select(any(.spec.parentRefs[]?; ((.namespace // $ns) + "/" + .name) | IN($g[]))) | . as $r | .spec.rules[]?.filters[]? | select(.type == "RequestRedirect") | "\($r.metadata.namespace)/\($r.metadata.name) scheme=\(.requestRedirect.scheme // "-") port=\(.requestRedirect.port // "default")"'  # redirects on an LBC ALB Gateway; port=default now follows the scheme (80/443), no longer the listener

title: The rule optimizer in v2.15.0 through v3.0.0 removed regex-based listener rules — land on v3.1.0 or newer when Ingresses use regexValues or use-regex-path-match

detection.reason: checked Ingresses for use-regex-path-match=true — the rules the optimizer dropped on every release from v2.15.0 to v3.0.0; conditions.* annotations with regexValues are a second, unchecked form

quote: [Ingress] Rule optimizer - Fixed incorrect removal of regex-based listener rules that could cause routing failures
remediation: Never land on v2.15.0–v3.0.0 with regex path rules: the optimizer (introduced in 2.15.0, fixed by #4484 in 3.1.0) removed them from the listener and requests fell through to the default action. Upgrade to v3.1.0+.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ingress -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select((.metadata.annotations["alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/use-regex-path-match"] // "" | test("true"; "i")) or ([.metadata.annotations | to_entries[] | select(.key | startswith("alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/conditions.")) | .value | test("regexValues")] | any)) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # Ingresses with regex listener rules; affected on v2.15.0 through v3.0.0
coversNotes: v3.1.0 (Documentation Updates): Fix rule optimizer incorrectly removing regex-based listener rul
